title: The other half: topic and comment
summary: Every sentence has a が carriage and also a は topic, visible or not. The comment after the topic is always a full logical clause.

blocks.text: Japanese has two structures at once. The **logical** one (carriage and engine) is ruled by **が**. The **non-logical** one (topic and comment) is ruled by **は**. A sentence always has a が carriage, and in the same way it always has a **は topic**, even when you cannot see it.

A topic is what the conversation is currently about. English tracks it with pronouns: "I had a ball. I dropped it. It rolled away. Sakura picked it up." The ball is sometimes an object, sometimes a subject, so what is tracked is not the subject but the topic. Japanese just tracks it with は, or leaves it out as a zero.
（私は）コーヒーが好きだ。 As for me, coffee is likable.

Sentences like コーヒーが好きだ, 頭が痛い, お腹が空いた and クレープが食べたい are complete logical clauses where the carriage is not the person. To be grammatically complete they also need an invisible topic: "in relation to me, coffee is likable". Usually the topic is "I", but not always. Seeing a tall person, you say 背が高いね, with an invisible topic pointing to that person.
The comment is a full clause

は can never mark the carriage or the engine, so a topic sentence has only **two** parts: the topic and the comment. Both elements of the logical clause must be **inside the comment**. So the comment is always a **complete logical clause**. This is not a random rule, but a consequence of the structure.
は or が is really a choice of what to show

People ask "は or が?" as if both did the same job. They do not. Since the topic and the carriage are both always present, you are really deciding which to make visible: neither (アメリカ人です), the topic (私はアメリカ人です), or the carriage (私がアメリカ人です). Each has a slightly different feeling.

blocks.en: As for elephants, the nose is long.
In this town, summer is hot.
As for me, the head hurts.

items: Two structures: **carriage + engine** (が) and **topic + comment** (は).
A topic can be invisible, just like a zero carriage.
The **comment** is always a full logical clause with its own carriage and engine.
は and が are not alternatives; they show different parts of the sentence.

questions.instruction: Which particle rules the non-logical side?
In 象は鼻が長い, what is the topic?
In 象は鼻が長い, what is the main carriage?
questions.note: が marks the carriage, the nose.
長い is the adjective engine.

questions.prompt: The comment after a は topic is always a complete logical clause.
questions.note: は cannot mark the carriage or engine, so both must sit in the comment.

questions.instruction: Why does 頭が痛い need an invisible topic?
options: The head belongs to someone: "as for me"

questions.instruction: Which fully shows both topic and carriage?
options: 私はコーヒーが好きだ。

questions.instruction: A tall person walks by. Which sentence fits?
questions.note: Invisible topic: the person; carriage: the height.

questions.instruction: The choice between は and が is really a choice of…
questions.note: Both the topic and the carriage are always there.

questions.instruction: How does English track a topic?
questions.note: That is why English uses many pronouns.

questions.prompt: In this town, summer is hot.

questions.instruction: In お腹が空いた, what is the invisible topic most likely?
questions.note: The stomach is the carriage; the topic is whose stomach it is.
